snippet.description:
Is "adulthood" a moving target? For millennials, hitting the milestones of the past—homeownership, secure careers, and financial independence—feels tougher  than ever. We aren't just having our individual midlife crises; we are simultaneously navigating an economic, cultural, and existential crisis, too.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

Guest host Jonquilyn Hill sits down with Amil Niazi, columnist at The Cut, to explore why this stage of life feels so precarious. From the domino effect of the 2008 financial crisis and the collapse of the traditional career path, to the pressures of the "sandwich generation" — caretaking for both children and aging parents — we break down why the millennial experience is fundamentally different from generations past.

00:00 Intro
01:43 The millennial economic domino effect
04:50 Redefining adulthood
07:45 Quarterlife vs midlife crisis
14:04 Is it late-stage capitalism?
21:42 The sandwich generation
38:24 Choosing optimism

Host: Jonquilyn Hill, host of Explain It To Me
Guest: Amil Niazi, columnist The Cut

Every UPSC aspirant knows the temptation: a new book, a new PDF, a new “must-read” source.

But does more content really mean better preparation?

AIR 100 Sattwik Satyakam shares what six attempts taught him about UPSC preparation: there are no reliable shortcuts. Instead of constantly chasing new sources, focus on revising a limited set of resources again and again, and test yourself until you know them thoroughly.

Sometimes, better preparation is not about finding more. It is about revising what you already have.
